answers.answer: Build the deck top to bottom as 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, then 4 Conflict III cards. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Top to bottom: 1x Conflict I, 5x Conflict II, 4x Conflict III”; unused cards are returned “without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and a third Agent (the Swordmaster) next to the board, not yet gained. Each has 12 troops: 3 in their garrison and 9 in supply; 1 water; and one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks. In a 3-player game each starts at 0 VP; in a 4-player game each starts at 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Setup: “2 Agents” on Leader, “third Agent (their Swordmaster) next to” board; 3 troops in garrison and “the rest” of 12 in supply; “takes 1 water”; cubes on bottom spaces; Score track 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may Reveal while Agents remain. After taking a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn later. Plot Intrigue may be played during your Reveal turn, but not later in the phase after that turn is over.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional and you “may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left”; after Reveal, turns “are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Plot cards may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and send one Agent to an unoccupied space showing an icon matching one Agent icon on that card. A card can send only one Agent; a card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn. Meet the space's requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving the space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “play one card,” choose only one matching Agent icon, “one card can't send multiple Agents”; space must be unoccupied; costs/requirements are paid immediately before effects.

answers.answer: No. The 4-spice Conspire cost must be paid before effects of the space or played card resolve, so 3 spice cannot be supplemented by spice gained from that card's Agent box. Once legally placed, the board-space effect and card's Agent-box effect may resolve in either order. The summary does not specify when the Faction Influence advancement must occur relative to those effects.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs are paid “before resolving any effects”; space plus Agent box resolve “in any order”; a Faction space also advances Influence one space. Board spaces: Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You may deploy at most 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn plus up to 2 more from your garrison. Any recruited troops you do not deploy remain in your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits go to your garrison and cannot normally be deployed through that action.
answers.evidence: Deploying: any or all troops recruited this turn “plus up to two more troops from your garrison”; recruits not deployed go to garrison. Rally Troops: “not a Combat space,” recruits go to garrison.

answers.answer: In order: (1) reveal all cards remaining in hand, separate from Agent-turn cards; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of the newly revealed cards, with purchases possible before, between, or after effects; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Only Reveal boxes of cards revealed for this Reveal turn are used, not the Reveal boxes of Agent-turn cards. At cleanup, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn steps 1–4; step 2 excludes cards played during Agent turns; step 4 puts all cards from Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, you may buy a replacement card after acquiring a Row card because the Imperium Row refills immediately, if you can afford it. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split one source across cards. Unspent Persuasion cannot be saved and is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. Acquired cards go to your discard pile and cannot be used immediately. An Acquire-box effect resolves once, at the moment you acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: Row refills immediately, Persuasion can be pooled or split, cannot be saved, acquired cards go to discard and “you don't use them right away”; Acquire effect is “at the moment you acquire the card.”

answers.answer: With 3 troops in the Conflict and 4 revealed swords, strength is 3×2 + 4 = 10. If your last troop is removed, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. For a value over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again at the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Set Strength: each Conflict troop is 2 and each revealed sword is 1; without a troop strength is 0 regardless of swords; over 20 use the +20 side and start again from track beginning.

answers.answer: During Combat, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Play proceeds from the First Player clockwise. A prior pass does not prevent playing later. Combat resolves once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. “When you win” cards are played only after you have won, before moving to the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: players with a troop may play or pass, First Player clockwise; passing earlier does not bind; resolve after consecutive passes; “when you win” cards follow winning and precede next phase.

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each takes the second reward. Since two players tied for first in a four-player game, C and D still compete for the third reward; because C beats D, C takes it and D gets nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward; a tie for third gives nothing. A player with 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply, not their garrison.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: first-place tie means no winner and tied players take second; in four-player game the other two compete for third; second-place tie gets third each, third-place tie nothing, 0 strength nothing; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: Normal harvesting happens when a player visits a space and resolves its effect: Imperial Basin gives 1 spice plus bonus spice, Hagga Basin 2 spice plus bonus, and The Great Flat 3 spice plus bonus. In Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, add 1 spice from the bank to each of these three Maker spaces that has no Agent, accumulating with any existing bonus. If an Agent moved away before Makers and the space is empty then, it receives the bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Makers phase checks The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin and adds spice where no Agent is present; Maker clarification says spice accumulates if an Agent moves away and the space is empty in Phase 4. Board-space table gives normal harvest amounts plus bonus.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately: the trigger is checked at the end of the round in Recall. The same end-of-round check applies if the last Conflict card has been revealed and the Conflict Deck is empty. Endgame Intrigue cards resolve before the winner is determined. The stated tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops. A further FAQ fallback after garrisoned troops is not provided in the summary.
answers.evidence: Recall checks 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck; Scoring says “at the end of a round” and Endgame Intrigue resolves first; tiebreakers list spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops. No later fallback is stated.

answers.answer: The VP from reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2; the summary does not explicitly state whether that VP is regained on returning to 2. The bonus earned at 4 Influence is kept after dropping below 4, and can be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. An Alliance is first taken by the first player to reach 4; it transfers, with its VP, if an opponent advances to a higher space. Merely tying the holder does not meet the stated transfer condition.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence gives VP “lost if you drop back below 2”; 4 bonus is not returned and can be earned again; Alliance goes to first at 4 and transfers if an opponent rises to a “higher space.”

answers.answer: The summary says an Alliance transfers if an opponent passes the holder by rising to a higher space. Here the opponents were already tied at 5, and the summary does not say what happens when the holder loses Influence or which opponent receives the Alliance if multiple opponents are already higher. If instead you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, the summary likewise does not explicitly address whether the Alliance transfers absent an opponent advancing; that outcome is unsupported by the summary.
answers.evidence: Alliance rule states transfer when an opponent passes the holder by rising to a higher space; it does not specify the outcome when the holder drops below already-tied opponents, or when the holder falls below 4 without an opponent advancing.

answers.answer: Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card is returned to its Reserve stack instead. Discarding sends a card to a discard pile (for example, cards in play go to your discard pile at cleanup); played Intrigue cards go face up next to the Intrigue Deck. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card directs you to trash it. You cannot reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffling occurs when unable to draw because the deck is empty.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: listed eligible locations and destinations, and optionality. Cleanup and Intrigue sections describe discard destinations. Deck exhaustion: reshuffle when unable to draw; “You can't reshuffle early” to look at the top card of an empty deck.

answers.answer: While you control Arrakeen or Carthag, you gain 1 Solari whenever any player (including you) sends an Agent there; Imperial Basin control pays 1 spice on any player's visit. Winning a Conflict that rewards control lets you place your marker on that space's flag, replacing an opponent's marker. When a later Conflict card is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the named Conflict places/replaces the marker; controller receives the listed bonus whenever any player visits; on a matching Conflict reveal, may deploy one troop from supply.

answers.answer: Two-player setup removes the three Arrakeen cards marked “1P”; the Rival's Influence cubes start at the bottoms of the tracks and it starts with no garrisoned troops. House Hagal is a third, spoiler Rival that acts after each First Player Agent turn while it has Agents. It takes Agent turns only and never Reveals. It does not collect resources, build a deck, earn rewards, score VP, or claim Control. Its exact starting Agent count is not stated in the summary. The general House Hagal rules say Influence icons can let a Rival take an Alliance if able, so it can hold an Alliance.
answers.evidence: Two-player setup and behavior are stated in the House Hagal section; general Rival rule says they take an Alliance if able. Starting number of Agents is not specified there.

answers.answer: For an occupied revealed space, keep revealing House Hagal cards until an unoccupied space is found. Reshuffle the House Hagal deck when empty or when the Reshuffle card appears. The Rival ignores normal space costs and effects and resolves only its card icons: each troop icon recruits one troop, deployed to the Conflict if the chosen space is a Combat space and otherwise placed in its garrison. In two-player Harvest Spice instructions remove bonus spice from the space to the bank. The summary does not explain how to choose between two applicable spaces on a card when one is occupied; it only says to keep revealing past occupied spaces.
answers.evidence: House Hagal: send to revealed space if unoccupied, “keep revealing past occupied spaces”; reshuffle when empty or Reshuffle card; ignore normal costs/effects; troop icons recruit and deploy/garrison by space; two-player Harvest Spice bonus goes to bank.

answers.answer: In Combat, each Rival with a troop in the Conflict reveals a House Hagal card and adds only its sword icons to strength. The Rival does not earn rewards in two-player play. If it wins a Conflict for a space another player controls, that Control marker is removed. Human second-place ties each take the third reward under the general tie rule, even though ordinary third place is unavailable in a two-player game. The summary does not state a separate two-player exception to that tie rule.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat: Rival reveals a card and counts only sword icons; two-player Rival “doesn't ... earn rewards” and removes another player's Control if it wins that space. General Combat ties: tied for second each receives third reward.
